\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{অপরাধ} (ôpôrādh)}{অপরাধ (ôpôrādh)}]{\bn{অপরাধ} (ôpôrādh) — a crime; an offence}

\label{lesson:BN-C283-oporadh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to push, then the Bengali for a pickpocket.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{অপরাধ}}
\textbf{\bn{অপরাধ}} — \emph{ôpôrādh} — \textquotedblleft{}a crime; an offence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{যদি} \bn{পুলিশ} \bn{তাড়াতাড়ি} \bn{না} \bn{আসে}, \bn{তাহলে} \bn{চোরেরা} \bn{আবার} \bn{অপরাধ} \bn{করবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jôdi pulish tāṛātāṛi nā āse, tāhôle chorerā ābār ôpôrādh kôrbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the police don't come quickly, the thieves will commit crimes again.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{অপরাধ}} (\emph{ôpôrādh}) is Sanskrit \emph{aparādha}, 'an offence, a transgression' (Monier-Williams), with \emph{apa-}, 'away': a going astray. \bn{অপরাধ} \bn{করা}, to commit a crime.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôpôrādh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôpôrādh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jôdi pulish tāṛātāṛi nā āse, tāhôle chorerā ābār ôpôrādh kôrbe.} — If the police don't come quickly, the thieves will commit crimes again.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to push, then the Bengali for a pickpocket, then say \emph{ôpôrādh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{অপরাধ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A crime; an offence\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{অভিযোগ} (ôbhijog)}{অভিযোগ (ôbhijog)}]{\bn{অভিযোগ} (ôbhijog) — a complaint; an accusation}

\label{lesson:BN-C283-obhijog}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a pickpocket, then the Bengali for a crime.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{অভিযোগ}}
\textbf{\bn{অভিযোগ}} — \emph{ôbhijog} — \textquotedblleft{}a complaint; an accusation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দোকানদার} \bn{থানায়} \bn{গিয়ে} \bn{অভিযোগ} \bn{করল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dokāndār thānāy giye ôbhijog kôrlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shopkeeper went to the police station and made a complaint.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{অভিযোগ}} (\emph{ôbhijog}) is Sanskrit \emph{abhiyoga}, 'an application, an earnest effort' (Monier-Williams); the sense 'a complaint, a charge' is the one Bengali uses. \bn{অভিযোগ} \bn{করা}, to complain.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôbhijog}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôbhijog}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dokāndār thānāy giye ôbhijog kôrlô.} — The shopkeeper went to the police station and made a complaint.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a pickpocket, then the Bengali for a crime, then say \emph{ôbhijog} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{অভিযোগ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A complaint; an accusation\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{গ্রেফতার} \bn{করা} (grephtār kôrā)}{গ্রেফতার করা (grephtār kôrā)}]{\bn{গ্রেফতার} \bn{করা} (grephtār kôrā) — to arrest}

\label{lesson:BN-C283-grephtar-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a crime, then the Bengali for a complaint.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{গ্রেফতার} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{গ্রেফতার} \bn{করা}} — \emph{grephtār kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to arrest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{পুলিশ} \bn{দুই} \bn{দিন} \bn{পরে} \bn{চোরকে} \bn{গ্রেফতার} \bn{করল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pulish dui din pôre chorke grephtār kôrlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police arrested the thief two days later.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{ডাকাতকে} \bn{গ্রেফতার} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini ḍākātke grephtār kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{গ্রেফতার} \bn{করা}} (\emph{grephtār kôrā}) puts \bn{গ্রেফতার} — usually traced to Persian \emph{giriftār}, 'taken, captured' — before \bn{করা}: to make someone a captive.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{grephtār kôrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{grephtār kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pulish dui din pôre chorke grephtār kôrlô.} — The police arrested the thief two days later.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a crime, then the Bengali for a complaint, then say \emph{grephtār kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{তদন্ত} (tôdôntô)}{তদন্ত (tôdôntô)}]{\bn{তদন্ত} (tôdôntô) — an investigation; an inquiry}

\label{lesson:BN-C283-todonto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a complaint, then the Bengali for to arrest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{তদন্ত}}
\textbf{\bn{তদন্ত}} — \emph{tôdôntô} — \textquotedblleft{}an investigation; an inquiry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{পুলিশ} \bn{ঘটনার} \bn{তদন্ত} \bn{শুরু} \bn{করল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pulish ghôṭônār tôdôntô shuru kôrlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police began an investigation into the incident.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{তদন্ত}} (\emph{tôdôntô}) is usually explained as Sanskrit \emph{tad}, 'that', and \emph{anta}, 'end': going to the end of a matter. Monier-Williams lists \emph{tadanta}, 'coming to an end by that'; the sense 'an inquiry' is the modern one.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tôdôntô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tôdôntô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pulish ghôṭônār tôdôntô shuru kôrlô.} — The police began an investigation into the incident.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a complaint, then the Bengali for to arrest, then say \emph{tôdôntô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{তদন্ত} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An investigation; an inquiry\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{দারোগা} (dārogā)}{দারোগা (dārogā)}]{\bn{দারোগা} (dārogā) — a police inspector}

\label{lesson:BN-C283-daroga}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to arrest, then the Bengali for an investigation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{দারোগা}}
\textbf{\bn{দারোগা}} — \emph{dārogā} — \textquotedblleft{}a police inspector\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{থানার} \bn{দারোগা} \bn{সাক্ষীকে} \bn{অনেক} \bn{প্রশ্ন} \bn{জিজ্ঞাসা} \bn{করলেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{thānār dārogā sākkhīke ônek prôshno jigyāsā kôrlen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The inspector at the station asked the witness a lot of questions.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{দারোগা}} (\emph{dārogā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{dārogha}, an overseer or chief officer; in Bengali it is the officer in charge of a police station.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dārogā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dārogā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{thānār dārogā sākkhīke ônek prôshno jigyāsā kôrlen.} — The inspector at the station asked the witness a lot of questions.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to arrest, then the Bengali for an investigation, then say \emph{dārogā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{দারোগা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A police inspector\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Something Happened to Crime and the Police}

\label{lesson:BN-R283-review-276-283}



\begin{quote}
Say the Bengali for an event and something.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item an event, something, many, a human being, an accident
  \item a witness, someone, everyone, a crowd, to turn up
  \item a jolt, to move, to break, to overturn, injured
  \item to be alight, a flame, a spark, to burn down, an explosion
  \item to arrive, to rescue, a ladder, a siren, refuge
  \item luckily, missing, to be spared, to rush, at last
  \item to steal, jewellery, to grab, to push, a pickpocket
  \item a crime, a complaint, to arrest, an investigation, a police inspector
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
An event? (\textbf{\bn{ঘটনা}}, \emph{ghôṭônā}.) Something? (\textbf{\bn{কিছু}}, \emph{kichhu}.) Many? (\textbf{\bn{অনেক}}, \emph{ônek}.) A human being? (\textbf{\bn{মানুষ}}, \emph{mānush}.) An accident? (\textbf{\bn{দুর্ঘটনা}}, \emph{durghôṭônā}.) A witness? (\textbf{\bn{সাক্ষী}}, \emph{sākkhī}.) Someone? (\textbf{\bn{কেউ}}, \emph{keu}.) Everyone? (\textbf{\bn{সবাই}}, \emph{sôbāi}.) A crowd? (\textbf{\bn{ভিড়}}, \emph{bhiṛ}.) To turn up? (\textbf{\bn{হাজির} \bn{হওয়া}}, \emph{hājir hôoyā}.) A jolt? (\textbf{\bn{ধাক্কা}}, \emph{dhākkā}.) To move? (\textbf{\bn{চলা}}, \emph{chôlā}.) To break? (\textbf{\bn{ভাঙা}}, \emph{bhāngā}.) To overturn? (\textbf{\bn{উল্টানো}}, \emph{ulṭāno}.) Injured? (\textbf{\bn{আহত}}, \emph{āhôtô}.) To be alight? (\textbf{\bn{জ্বলা}}, \emph{jvôlā}.) A flame? (\textbf{\bn{শিখা}}, \emph{shikhā}.) A spark? (\textbf{\bn{স্ফুলিঙ্গ}}, \emph{sphulinggô}.) To burn down? (\textbf{\bn{পুড়ে} \bn{যাওয়া}}, \emph{puṛe jāoyā}.) An explosion? (\textbf{\bn{বিস্ফোরণ}}, \emph{bisphorôn}.) To arrive? (\textbf{\bn{পৌঁছানো}}, \emph{poũchhāno}.) To rescue? (\textbf{\bn{উদ্ধার} \bn{করা}}, \emph{uddhār kôrā}.) A ladder? (\textbf{\bn{মই}}, \emph{môi}.) A siren? (\textbf{\bn{সাইরেন}}, \emph{sāiren}.) Refuge? (\textbf{\bn{আশ্রয়}}, \emph{āshrôy}.) Luckily? (\textbf{\bn{ভাগ্যক্রমে}}, \emph{bhāgyôkrôme}.) Missing? (\textbf{\bn{নিখোঁজ}}, \emph{nikhõj}.) To be spared? (\textbf{\bn{রক্ষা} \bn{পাওয়া}}, \emph{rôkkhā pāoyā}.) To rush? (\textbf{\bn{ছোটা}}, \emph{chhoṭā}.) At last? (\textbf{\bn{অবশেষে}}, \emph{ôbôsheshe}.) To steal? (\textbf{\bn{চুরি} \bn{করা}}, \emph{churi kôrā}.) Jewellery? (\textbf{\bn{গয়না}}, \emph{gôynā}.) To grab? (\textbf{\bn{পাকড়ানো}}, \emph{pākṛāno}.) To push? (\textbf{\bn{ঠেলা}}, \emph{ṭhelā}.) A pickpocket? (\textbf{\bn{পকেটমার}}, \emph{pôkeṭmār}.) A crime? (\textbf{\bn{অপরাধ}}, \emph{ôpôrādh}.) A complaint? (\textbf{\bn{অভিযোগ}}, \emph{ôbhijog}.) To arrest? (\textbf{\bn{গ্রেফতার} \bn{করা}}, \emph{grephtār kôrā}.) An investigation? (\textbf{\bn{তদন্ত}}, \emph{tôdôntô}.) A police inspector? (\textbf{\bn{দারোগা}}, \emph{dārogā}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
